projects.name: Kanigiri Restaurant
projects.result: Live demo — dish carousel, full menu & reviews on one page
projects.desc: A single-page restaurant site for Kanigiri Restaurant — Mutton Biryani hero, a dish carousel, the full menu and reviews, all on one page.
projects.story: Open the demo to browse the menu and dishes. It is a one-page site, so everything — hero, dishes, menu and reviews — sits on the home page.
deliverables: Dish carousel with Mutton Biryani hero
projects.bestFor: Andhra restaurant owners who want customers to browse the biryani menu, order online and book a table without calling.
projects.summary: Kanigiri is a restaurant demo site built around an Andhra menu: biryanis, rice, curries and breads with spice levels, a Veg-only filter and search, plus online ordering, table booking, offers and reviews. Everything runs in the browser as a working demo — you can fill a cart and start an order, but no real food is ordered and no payment is taken.
projects.problem: A typical small-town restaurant problem: the menu lives on a phone photo or a food-app listing, so regulars cannot see prices or spice levels before they order; orders come through apps that take a cut, and table bookings arrive by phone during the lunch rush. Offers and loyalty live nowhere, so repeat customers get nothing for coming back. This is a demo scenario for this kind of business — Kanigiri is not a real restaurant and had no real customer problem to solve.

approach.decision: One menu-led site where ordering, table booking and offers sit on the same pages as the dishes, instead of sending customers to food apps.
approach.why: Regulars decide what to eat first and only then think about ordering or booking. Keeping the whole journey next to the menu means fewer steps between a dish and an order, and the restaurant keeps the direct-order saving instead of paying app commission.

approach.decision: Spice levels, a Veg-only filter and search on the menu, so a customer can find a dish that fits their taste in seconds.
approach.why: Andhra food is spicy, and spice tolerance varies from table to table. Labelling heat and filtering by Veg answers the two questions every customer asks before they order anything.

approach.decision: Ordering stays a browser demo with a clear mock note and no payment step, and offers are labelled mock too.
approach.why: The demo exists to show the ordering flow, not to take money or promise discounts. A real restaurant would connect its own ordering, payment and offer system, and set its own prices.

includes: Menu with spice levels and Veg filter
Online ordering with cart (demo, no payment)

approach.why: The point is to show parents the flow — look up a ward, check the term summary, pay — without anyone risking a real payment or real pupil data.

approach.decision: A Hindi version of the home page and a six-stop virtual tour sit beside the English pages, not behind a download.
approach.why: Many parents read Hindi first, and many families cannot visit before applying, so the tour and the Hindi page answer their first questions from home.

posts.title: Your shop is on Google already. The question is what people find.
posts.excerpt: Customers search before they visit. If the search shows a wrong timing, a dead page, or your competitor — that is the visit you lost.
body: Open Google and search for your own business the way a stranger would — your service plus your area. Whatever appears is your shop window for most new customers, whether you built it or not.

For many small businesses that window is a half-empty listing, an old phone number, and a competitor right below with photos, timings and a website. The fix is not complicated: correct details everywhere, real photos, and one page of your own that answers the questions customers actually ask.
A website you own is the one result nobody can edit but you. Prices, timings, photos, offers — current, because keeping them current is part of the job you hand to us.

posts.title: WhatsApp is your real checkout. Your website should know that.
posts.excerpt: Indian customers do not want another app or a payment form for a ₹400 cake. They want to tap a button and talk to you. Build for that.
body: Watch how your customers already buy: they ask on WhatsApp, you confirm, they pay when they collect or by UPI. The conversation is the checkout — it is personal, and it works.

So a small business website should not copy a big e-commerce store. It should show everything clearly — photos, names, prices — and put a WhatsApp button on every item, opening a chat with the order already written.
That is how every Kumbuild catalogue is built. No commission, no new habits for your customers, and you keep the relationship that makes them come back.

posts.title: What should a small business website actually cost?
posts.excerpt: Quotes range from ₹2,000 to ₹2,00,000 and all call themselves 'a website'. Here is what the money really buys at each level.
body: A website quote buys four things: the design, the writing and photos, the technical setup (domain, hosting, security), and the care afterwards. When a quote is very cheap, one of the four is missing — usually the last two, which fail quietly months later.

Agencies charge for account managers and offices. Freelancers charge less but disappear. A fixed-package service like Kumbuild charges for the work itself: the pages are defined, the price is on the website, and the renewal covers hosting, security and small changes.
Whichever route you take, ask three questions before paying: What exactly is included? What does year two cost? And if I leave, what do I take with me? The answers tell you the real price.

landing-page.d: Built for the link in your Instagram or Facebook bio. One page, one job: a visitor lands, sees your best work and taps to order on WhatsApp.

booking-website.d: Let customers book a table, a chair or an appointment from your website — requests land on your WhatsApp, confirmed by you. No commissions, no middlemen.

catalogue-website.d: Your full catalogue or menu on one fast page — photos, prices and a WhatsApp order button on every item. Update prices anytime with one message to us.

shops-stores.t: Websites for shops & stores — more footfall
shops-stores.d: Customers check prices and offers on their phone before they visit — or instead of visiting. Your website shows what you sell, at what price, first.

clinics-doctors.d: Before they call, patients want to know what you treat, when you are available and what it costs. Your website answers all three, clearly.

tuition-coaching.d: Parents compare courses, batches and fees online before they ever visit. Your website lays it all out — and takes admission enquiries on WhatsApp.

salons-parlours.t: Websites for salons & parlours — more bookings
salons-parlours.d: Your phone rings most when every stylist has a client in the chair. Your website answers prices and timings, and takes bookings while you work.

restaurants-cafes.d: Customers check the menu on their phone before they arrive — or before they order in. Your website shows the menu, photos, timings and location.

instagram-home-sellers.d: Your Instagram bio gets one link. Make it a page that shows your products, your prices and a WhatsApp order button — open all day, every day.
